title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List
prompt:
Given the `head` of a sorted singly linked list, delete all duplicate values so that each element appears only once, and return the resulting sorted list.

The list is given as an array (e.g. `[1,1,2,3,3]` represents `1 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 3 -> null`). The starter code includes helpers to convert between the array and a linked-list node — build the actual list, remove duplicates by manipulating `next` pointers, then convert back to an array to return.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 300]
The list is guaranteed to be sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: Because the list is sorted, all duplicates of a value are guaranteed to sit next to each other.
Walk a single pointer through the list, comparing each node to the one after it.
While the next node has the same value as the current node, skip over it; otherwise advance to the next node.

solution.approach: Since the list is sorted, duplicate values always appear consecutively, so a single forward pass suffices. Walk a pointer `curr` through the list; while curr.next exists and shares curr's value, splice it out via curr.next = curr.next.next. Otherwise, advance curr. This leaves exactly one node per distinct value.
